args.message:
Implement banker's rounding in round_money per FIN-212

round_money documented ROUND_HALF_EVEN but used ROUND_HALF_UP,
causing tests/test_money.py to fail. Switch to ROUND_HALF_EVEN.

args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix banker's rounding in round_money per FIN-212
args.body:
## Summary
`round_money` documented banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212) but implemented ROUND_HALF_UP, causing the nightly build failure in tests/test_money.py.

## Changes
- Import and use ROUND_HALF_EVEN in src/money.py instead of ROUND_HALF_UP.

## Verification
- CI run ci-0001 on fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding (08d3cd5986) passed.

Nights build should turn green once this merges.

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

- **Root cause:** `src/money.py` imported and used `ROUND_HALF_UP` while its docstring (and FIN-212, and the test) required banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`) — the test asserting `2.665 → 2.66` failed because half-up yields `2.67`.
- **Fix:** Created branch `fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding` and changed the rounding mode to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` in `round_money`.
- **CI:** Triggered run `ci-0001`, which passed (sha `08d3cd5986`).
- **PR:** Opened PR #101 against main with @alex as the requested reviewer: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

Note: per policy I have not merged anything into main — the merge awaits review/approval.

transcript.reasoning_content: Let me look at the repo files first.

transcript.content: The bug is confirmed: `round_money` imports and uses `ROUND_HALF_UP` instead of the documented `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. Let me fix it on a new branch.
transcript.reasoning_content: Interesting: test expects 2.675 → 2.68. With ROUND_HALF_EVEN, 2.675 in binary... Decimal is exact, so 2.675 → half even → 2.68 (since 7 odd → 8). Actually 2.675 quantize to 2 decimals: 2.675 → third digit 5, even rounding: 2.68 because 7 is odd → round up to 8. And 2.665 → .66 because 6 is even. So ROUND_HALF_EVEN satisfies both. Wait, but with ROUND_HALF_UP, 2.665 → 2.67, fails. So fix: change import and rounding mode.
